subject.title: Google Chat: Add user OAuth support for reactions and media uploads

question: Should the bundled Google Chat plugin add a first-class user OAuth credential surface for reactions, uploads, reaction typing, and proactive DM/email-alias lookup now, or should OpenClaw continue with service-account-only behavior plus narrower fallbacks?
rationale: The requested change adds new credential/config surface, refresh-token handling, OAuth scope routing, and user-identity behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent auth boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve plugin-owned user OAuth
options.body: Implement OAuth inside the Google Chat plugin with SecretRef/redaction support, scoped clients, docs, absent-OAuth fallback behavior, and fresh-install plus upgrade tests.

options.title: Limit current work to fallbacks
options.body: Land or close the media-link fallback PRs separately and leave native uploads, reactions, reaction typing, and proactive DMs unsupported until a broader OAuth design is sponsored.

options.title: Defer bundled OAuth
options.body: Keep bundled Google Chat service-account-only and ask for an external plugin or ClawHub package if maintainers do not want this credential model in the bundled plugin yet.

recommendation.title: Approve plugin-owned user OAuth
recommendation.body: Implement OAuth inside the Google Chat plugin with SecretRef/redaction support, scoped clients, docs, absent-OAuth fallback behavior, and fresh-install plus upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete posted the prior maintainer-side review on this issue and appears as a recent reviewer/committer across the Google Chat auth/API/docs surface.
